SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for the past three days.
- Onset: Started three days ago, initially with vomiting (a couple of times), which has now resolved; ongoing watery, loose stools.
- Frequency: Diarrhea 5-6 times per day.
- Associated symptoms: Initial vomiting (now resolved), feelings of dehydration, poor oral intake (reduced appetite, difficulty tolerating fluids), general weakness, felt slightly febrile at onset (currently afebrile), no abdominal pain, no blood in stools, no headaches or muscle pains.
- Aggravating/relieving factors: None stated.
- Past medical history: Asthma.
- Medications: Blue inhaler for asthma (dose/route/frequency not documented), used infrequently.
- Allergies: None known.
- Social history: Lives alone; works as a software engineer; not currently working due to illness; drinks alcohol infrequently/socially; does not smoke.
- Family history: Father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer; mother has type 2 diabetes.

Objective:
- No physical exam or vital sign findings documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Diarrhea (Acute Watery Diarrhea)
   - Assessment: Likely gastroenteritis.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not documented.
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Advise increased oral fluid intake.
     - Oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) recommended.
     - Symptomatic management with paracetamol for fever/weakness.
     - Time off work recommended until 24-48 hours diarrhea-free before return.
     - Safety net: advised to return if symptoms persist beyond a week or worsen.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: No physical exam or vital signs documented; no stool description beyond "watery"; no lab investigations.
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
● Transcript quality: Clear, minimal background noise; no issues with audibility.
